title: Minions Crash the Box Office with Monster-Sized Laughs!
summary: The Minions are back, and they're making movies — literally! In their new film 'Minions & Monsters,' the banana-loving goofballs travel to the 1920s to become filmmakers. Their big idea? Find real monsters to star in a scary creature feature. On Friday, the movie earned a whopping $16 million in North America, zooming straight to #1. By the end of the weekend, it could gobble up $39.5 million. That might sound huge, but for Minions, it's actually a bit of a slow start. Their last solo adventure, 'Minions: The Rise of Gru' in 2022, made almost a billion dollars worldwide! Still, with $87 million expected from other countries by Sunday, these little yellow stars are far from flops. Right behind them is 'Toy Story 5,' which added $13 million on Friday. Woody and Buzz have been in theaters for three weeks and already have $367 million in North America. The Toy Story gang is chasing the record set by 'Toy Story 4,' which made over $1 billion. In third place, a movie about young George Washington fighting in the Revolutionary War earned $7.4 million. Meanwhile, 'Supergirl' had a rough day, dropping 76% from last weekend. Ouch! So if you're looking for laughs this weekend, the Minions are ready to roll — and maybe even direct!
why_it_matters: Watching how movies perform shows us what stories people enjoy, and it’s a reminder that even silly characters can bring joy to millions.

background_read: The Minions (small, yellow characters who love bananas and serve the villain Gru) first appeared in the 2010 film Despicable Me and became so popular they got their own movies.
The 1920s, where this new Minion adventure takes place, was a decade when silent movies were being replaced by talkies, and monster films like Dracula and Frankenstein first scared audiences.
The film about young George Washington is set during the Revolutionary War (the war in the late 1700s where the American colonies fought to become their own country).
Article_Structure: WHO: The Minions, Woody and Buzz, and young George Washington.
WHAT: 'Minions & Monsters' earned $16 million on Friday, leading the box office, while 'Toy Story 5' followed and 'Supergirl' dropped sharply.
WHY: Because Minions are hugely popular worldwide, though this opening was slower than previous Minion films.

perspectives.description: Minions delight audiences with goofy slapstick humor; families love sharing laughs together in the theater.
Some might say this Minion opening isn’t as strong as past films, and the banana-loving creatures could be losing their charm.
Box office numbers can change fast, and strong earnings from other countries could still make it a big worldwide hit.
